Commentary of al-Qasimi (Mahasin al-Ta'wil) on surah 101, verses 1–5:

(p-6241) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

Surah al-Qari'ah

Meccan, and its number of verses is eleven.

(p-6242) In the name of Allah, the Most Gracious, the Most Merciful.

On the interpretation of His, may He be exalted, statement:

[1–5] ﴿The Striking Calamity﴾ ﴿What is the Striking Calamity?﴾ [al-Qari'ah: 2] ﴿And what will make you know what the Striking Calamity is?﴾ [al-Qari'ah: 3] ﴿It is a Day when mankind will be like scattered moths﴾ [al-Qari'ah: 4] ﴿And the mountains will be like wool, fluffed up﴾ [al-Qari'ah: 5]

﴿The Striking Calamity﴾ ﴿What is the Striking Calamity?﴾ [al-Qari'ah: 2]. Abu al-Su'ud said: al-qar' (striking) is striking with force and vehemence, such that a loud sound results from it. It is the Resurrection (al-qiyamah), and it was named thus because it strikes hearts and ears with all kinds of terror and horrors, and it brings all the celestial and terrestrial bodies from one state to another: the heaven by splitting and cleaving, the sun and stars by being folded up, dimmed and scattered, the earth by quaking and being changed, and the mountains by being crushed and blown away.

It is a subject (mubtada') whose predicate (khabar) is His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿What is the Striking Calamity?﴾ [al-Qari'ah: 2], with (ma) the interrogative being the predicate and al-qari'ah the subject, and not the reverse, because the locus of benefit is the predicate, not the subject. There is no doubt that the focus of conveying awe and magnitude here is the word (ma), not (al-qari'ah); i.e., what wondrous thing is it in its magnitude and dreadfulness? The apparent noun has been placed in the position of the pronoun for emphasis on the awesomeness.

His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿And what will make you know what the Striking Calamity is?﴾ [al-Qari'ah: 3] is an emphasis on its terror and dreadfulness, by declaring its departure from the circle of the knowledge of creation, in the sense that its great status and extent of severity are such that the comprehension of anyone barely attains it, until it is made known to you by it; i.e., what thing has made you know the affair of the Striking Calamity? Since this was foretold as a generous promise of informing you of it, He fulfilled that with His statement, may He be exalted: ﴿It is a Day when mankind will be like scattered moths﴾ [al-Qari'ah: 4], i.e., it is a day on which mankind will be like scattered moths in multitude and dispersal, in weakness, lowliness and agitation, and flying toward the caller, like moths flying into the fire. (p-6243) So "yawma" (the day) is the predicate of an omitted subject, built on fatha because it is attached to a verb, or it is in the accusative by an implied (udhkur, "mention"), as if it were said, after magnifying the matter of the Striking Calamity and arousing eagerness in him, peace be upon him, to know it: Mention the day when mankind will be...

﴿And the mountains will be like wool, fluffed up﴾ [al-Qari'ah: 5], i.e., like carded wool, in the scattering of their parts and their being blown about in the air. Since it is known that that day is the day on which the Hereafter life begins, and in it the measures of deeds and what they deserve of recompense are known, He arranged upon it His statement, may He be exalted:

The Interpretation of His Words, Exalted Is He:

[6–11] ﴿As for him whose scales are heavy﴾ ﴿he will be in a pleasing life﴾ [al-Qari'ah: 7] ﴿And as for him whose scales are light﴾ [al-Qari'ah: 8] ﴿his mother will be the Abyss﴾ [al-Qari'ah: 9] ﴿And what can make you know what that is?﴾ [al-Qari'ah: 10] ﴿A Fire, intensely hot!﴾ [al-Qari'ah: 11]

﴿As for him whose scales are heavy﴾ ﴿he will be in a pleasing life﴾ [al-Qari'ah: 7]. Ibn Jarir said: That is, as for him whose scales of good deeds are heavy. By "scales" he means the weighing. The Arabs say: "I have a dirham for you by the scale of your dirham" (lakа ʿindī dirham bi-mīzān dirhamika), and they say: "My house is by the scale of your house and its weight" (dārī bi-mīzān dārika wa-wazn dārika), meaning: opposite your house. The poet said:

"I was, before meeting you, one of strength; for every adversary I have his scale."

By his saying "his scale" (mīzānuhu) he means his speech and that by which he refutes his argument. Mujahid used to say: It is not a scale; it is a parable that was struck. End of quote.

Accordingly, the "mawazin" (scales) is the plural of "mizan" (scale). It is also permitted that it be the plural of "mawzun" (weighed), meaning the deed that has weight and worth with God, Exalted is He. As for his saying, "in a pleasing life" (fī ʿīshatin rāḍiyah), it means: in a life that He has approved of in Paradise. So "rāḍiyah" (pleasing) is in the sense of "marḍiyyah" (approved), either by a figurative usage in the word itself or in its attribution, or it is a metaphor (istiʿārah) that is implicit (makniyyah) and imaginative (takhyīliyyah).

﴿And as for him whose scales are light﴾ [al-Qari'ah: 8]: that is, the weight of his good deeds is light.

﴿his mother will be the Abyss﴾ [al-Qari'ah: 9]: that is, his refuge and dwelling is the Abyss (hawiyah), into which he will fall headfirst into Hell.

Al-Shihab said: He named the refuge "mother" by way of comparison and mockery, because the mother of a child is his refuge and resting place. In "al-Ta'wilat" it is said: It has been said that the intended meaning is "mother of his head", that is, he will be cast into the Fire upside down on his head. End of quote.

The first view is the one consistent with His saying: ﴿And what can make you know what that is?﴾ [al-Qari'ah: 10] ﴿A Fire, intensely hot!﴾ [al-Qari'ah: 11], for it is an explanation of it after its vagueness, and an indication of its going beyond the familiar limits, for the sake of awe. The original form of "mā hiyah" (what it is) is "mā hiya", a periphrasis for the Abyss; the silent hā' (hā' al-sakt) was added at its end in pausal pronunciation. It is dropped in connected speech, though it has been permitted to retain it in connected speech as well.

It is also permitted that it be the plural of "mawzun" (weighed), meaning the deed that has weight and worth with God, Exalted is He. So "rāḍiyah" (pleasing) is in the sense of "marḍiyyah" (approved), either by a figurative usage in the word itself or in its attribution, or it is a metaphor (istiʿārah) that is implicit (makniyyah) and imaginative (takhyīliyyah).

Al-Shihab said: He named the refuge "mother" by way of comparison and mockery, because the mother of a child is his refuge and resting place. In "al-Ta'wilat" it is said: It has been said that the intended meaning is "mother of his head", that is, he will be cast into the Fire upside down on his head. End of quote.

The first view is the one consistent with His saying: ﴿And what can make you know what that is?﴾ [al-Qari'ah: 10] ﴿A Fire, intensely hot!﴾ [al-Qari'ah: 11], for it is an explanation of it after its vagueness, and an indication of its going beyond the familiar limits, for the sake of awe. It is dropped in connected speech, though it has been permitted to retain it in connected speech as well.
